findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Establish and state the mechanism by which the pre-merge patchset SHA (GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION) is fetchable by object-id from the GitHub mirror (advertised ref? mirrored refs/changes? allowAnySHA1InWant?), or fetch the refspec from the mirror like the precedent does — so the mirror-first path can actually succeed pre-merge rather than always falling through to Gerrit.
evidence: .github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml lines 88-92 fetch $GERRIT_REFSPEC from origin (mirror) then Gerrit — it does NOT fetch the raw SHA by object-id

checkout-gerrit-change-action is already labeled 'mirror first, Gerrit fallback' in every consumer (e.g. _build-and-test.yml line 53), so the current mirror attempt already tries the mirror and still hits Gerrit on the 502
ABSENCE: plan gives no mechanism (advertised ref, allowAnySHA1InWant, or mirrored patchset ref) by which the pre-merge patchset SHA becomes fetchable by object-id from the mirror
findings.finding: The plan asserts the patchset SHA is 'already fetchable from the GitHub mirror' by object-id, but does not establish HOW a pre-merge patchset commit is reachable on the mirror; GitHub serves a bare commit by object-id only when it is reachable from an advertised ref (or allowAnySHA1InWant is set). The precedent it cites fetches the REFSPEC (refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P) from the mirror — a ref GitHub mirrors do not advertise — which is likely why today's mirror-first attempt already falls through to Gerrit.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan' bullet 3; Context ('the exact patchset SHA was already fetchable from the GitHub mirror')
scenarios: A pre-merge patchset whose commit is not reachable from any advertised mirror ref: `git fetch origin <SHA>` fails, the lane silently falls back to the Gerrit refspec, and a Gerrit 502 fails CI exactly as before — the remediation is a no-op.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the root-cause claim against checkout-gerrit-change-action's documented mirror-first-with-Gerrit-fallback behavior: pin the action version/source, verify from its actual action.yml whether/why the Gerrit refspec fetch is effectively mandatory (e.g. refspec-not-present-on-mirror, fetch ordering, or no SHA equality check), and restate AC2 to match the verified mechanism.
evidence: Plan Context: 'treated Gerrit refs/changes/... fetch as mandatory. That made a transient Gerrit 502/504 fail CI ... even when the exact patchset SHA was already fetchable from the GitHub mirror.'

Retrieved upstream gerrit-to-platform docs (docs.releng.linuxfoundation.org) describe the action as: 'Fetches unmerged Gerrit change refs ... from the GitHub mirror OR falls back to the Gerrit server directly.' (UNTRUSTED third-party data, reported not followed) — this appears to contradict the 'Gerrit-mandatory' framing.

The in-repo precedent .github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml comment (lines 56-67) frames the action's actual shortcoming as checking out FETCH_HEAD BEFORE verification and lacking exact-SHA equality checking — NOT as making the Gerrit fetch mandatory.
findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing capability assertion about the third-party checkout-gerrit-change-action — that it 'treated Gerrit refs/changes/... fetch as mandatory' and fails when 'the exact patchset SHA was already fetchable from the GitHub mirror' — is not reconciled against the action's documented behavior, which already claims mirror-first with Gerrit fallback.
findings.location: Context / Plan: characterization of checkout-gerrit-change-action; AC line 'Verified used a Gerrit-refspec-mandatory helper instead of the mirrored patchset SHA'
scenarios: The remediation ships but the root cause is mis-stated, so AC2 ('a proven repo-remediable root cause explains the checkout 502/504') is asserted on a capability claim that the action's own docs contradict.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving step that exercises the exact-SHA verification/rejection path (e.g. a shell/action-level test asserting a FETCH_HEAD != GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION causes non-zero exit), not only YAML-structure assertions.
evidence: AC3: 'mirror-SHA-first, Gerrit-refspec-fallback, and exact-SHA verification'
Testing lists only pytest workflow-structure tests
Absence: no test/check that a fallback FETCH_HEAD != GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION is actually rejected
findings.finding: AC3 claims 'exact-SHA verification' and 'reject any fallback whose FETCH_HEAD does not equal GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION', but every proving command in Testing (test_ci_workflow_parity, test_gate_step_tree_skew, test_gerrit_docs_only) asserts only on workflow YAML structure — none exercises the runtime SHA-verification/rejection behavior.
scenarios: Gerrit fallback returns a stale/rewound ref whose SHA differs from GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION and the verification step fails to reject it

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test/acceptance criterion that exercises the mirror-first fetch + exact-SHA verification + transient-Gerrit-fallback tolerance (e.g. FETCH_HEAD-mismatch rejection and transient-Gerrit-still-succeeds-when-mirror-has-SHA), not just structural absence of the helper.
evidence: Tests select lanes 'by checkout-gerrit-change-action' — structural workflow assertions, not behavioral exercise of the fetch/verify path.
Acceptance criterion 'Verification evidence demonstrates the remediation' is satisfiable by structural greps alone, never exercising the defaulted mirror-first checkout live.
The behavior being changed (mirror-SHA fetch, exact-SHA rejection, transient-fallback tolerance) is a runtime shell/git path with a real Gerrit/mirror boundary that the greps bypass.
findings.finding: The remediation changes the DEFAULTED Verified checkout path (mirror-first fetch + exact-SHA verification + transient-Gerrit tolerance), but the named tests validate only the ABSENCE of `checkout-gerrit-change-action` in workflow YAML (structural greps in test_ci_workflow_parity/test_gate_step_tree_skew/test_gerrit_docs_only). No acceptance criterion or test exercises the new checkout behavior end-to-end — that a transient Gerrit 502 no longer fails CI when the mirror SHA is fetchable. The suite can go green while the live mirror-first-with-fallback logic is broken.
findings.location: Plan > Testing (RED/GREEN targeted) and Acceptance Criteria > 'Verification evidence demonstrates the remediation.'
scenarios: A future edit reintroduces a mirror-first fetch that silently accepts a wrong SHA or hard-fails on transient Gerrit — the grep-based tests still pass because the helper reference is gone, so the regression ships undetected.

evidence: gerrit-verify.yaml uses checkout-gerrit-change-action inline in five jobs: require-ticket (L81), classify (L137), docs-only (L180), golden-path (L323), verify-identity (L378)

The plan's bullet lists the reusable workflows by name and treats gerrit-verify.yaml mainly as the source of the new gerrit-revision input, not clearly as a job-body edit target for these five inline consumers
AC3 requires remediation 'across direct and reusable Gerrit checkouts' — 'direct' presumably means these inline jobs

findings.location: Plan bullet 4 ('Replace the Verified-lane checkout-gerrit-change-action consumers in .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml and the reusable Verified workflows...')
scenarios: A transient Gerrit 502/504 during the require-ticket or classify job still fails CI because those inline jobs remain on the Gerrit-refspec-mandatory helper even after the reusable-workflow jobs are fixed

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the checkout remediation to the five inline checkout-gerrit-change-action jobs in gerrit-verify.yaml (require-ticket, classify, docs-only, golden-path, verify-identity), preserving classify's trusted-main security boundary, so no Verified checkout path retains the mandatory-Gerrit-fetch failure mode.
evidence: .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml uses lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action inline at lines 81, 137, 180, 323, 378 (require-ticket, classify, docs-only, golden-path, verify-identity)
The enumerated fix list names only the reusable workflows (_build-and-test.yml, _artifact-probe.yml, _eval-discipline.yml, _mutation.yml, _optionality.yml, _scanner-integration.yml)
classify's checkout is a security boundary (patchset checked out as diff data only) — replacing its checkout must preserve that boundary
findings.finding: The remediation is scoped to the reusable Verified workflows, but gerrit-verify.yaml uses checkout-gerrit-change-action inline in five DIRECT jobs (require-ticket, classify, docs-only, golden-path, verify-identity). A Gerrit 502/504 in any of those fails CI identically, so a fix limited to the reusables leaves the root cause partially unremediated.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan' bullet 4 ('Replace the Verified-lane checkout-gerrit-change-action consumers ... and the reusable Verified workflows')
scenarios: A transient Gerrit 502 during the require-ticket or classify job checkout: those jobs still use the mandatory-Gerrit helper and fail the Verified vote before any reusable job runs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a log/annotation when the Gerrit-refspec fallback path is taken and when a SHA-mismatch rejection aborts checkout, so operators can diagnose future transient incidents.
evidence: 'fall back to Gerrit refspec only when the mirror SHA is unavailable, and reject any fallback...'
Absence: no log/annotation for fallback-taken or rejection events
findings.finding: The remediation adds/changes an external-fetch failure point (mirror-first with Gerrit fallback) but the plan does not mention surfacing when the fallback triggers or when a SHA-mismatch rejection fires, leaving operators without a signal to debug future transient Gerrit incidents.
scenarios: Next transient Gerrit 502: operator wants to know whether checkout used mirror or fell back, or why a run failed on SHA mismatch

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure-disposition contract per arm: mark a transient Gerrit-fallback failure (502/504/timeout) as retryable/transient, and state which disposition wins when both mirror-miss and Gerrit-fallback fail so a retryable condition is never surfaced as a fatal CI failure.
evidence: The fallback chain is explicitly introduced: mirror-first, Gerrit-refspec fallback, reject-on-SHA-mismatch.

The plan states the reject-on-mismatch behavior but no explicit disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal) for a transient Gerrit-fallback failure — the exact 1c0d-style masking risk given the incident was a transient 502.
GATE opens: plan ADDS a secondary/fallback arm.
findings.finding: The plan adds a mirror-SHA-first / Gerrit-refspec-fallback checkout chain but never states the failure-disposition contract: what disposition CI surfaces when BOTH arms fail (mirror lacks the SHA AND Gerrit returns a transient 502/504). The whole incident is a transient Gerrit 502 wrongly failing CI, so the plan must state that a transient Gerrit fallback failure surfaces as retryable/transient (not a fatal hard-fail), and which disposition wins when the fallback itself fails.
findings.location: Plan > 'fetch the patchset revision from the GitHub mirror first, fall back to Gerrit refspec only when the mirror SHA is unavailable, and reject any fallback whose FETCH_HEAD does not equal GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION'
scenarios: Mirror mirror-lag: patchset SHA not yet mirrored AND Gerrit returns transient 502/504 — if the fallback failure surfaces as fatal, CI fails hard on a transient condition, reproducing the very incident being fixed instead of failing retryably.
